description:
File:crate-jmap-chat-server/src/space.rs:714
Issue: The post-write duplicate-member dedup filter (lines 714-730) removes the first occurrence of account_id in post_members, not necessarily the entry this racer wrote. In a two-racer scenario, both racers see duplicate_count > 1 and both attempt to remove one entry. Their two cleanup writes (both update_object with a deduped slice) race again. The winning write determines final state, which can be: (a) 0 members if both removed the same (surviving) entry, or (b) 1 member from an arbitrary racer. In case (a) neither racer has a membership and both return serverFail/retry, but after retry no membership exists to be found — the join silently fails to persist.
Impact: Under concurrent Space/join for the same account, membership can be permanently lost: both racers fail, the space is left with no member entry for the joining account, and a subsequent join by the same account will appear to succeed but find no pre-existing entry to deduplicate. The race window is small but real; the storage layer unique-constraint (mentioned in the comment) is the only safe guard.
Fix: Instead of removing the first occurrence, identify which entry this racer wrote (by comparing joinedAt to now_str, or by storing the entry value before writing and matching it exactly) and remove only that entry. Alternatively, filter by the exact member object rather than by id-only equality, using the timestamp as a tiebreaker.
title: Space/join TOCTOU dedup removes wrong entry
